newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Ancient statuette might be sign of Albania temple.
newsitem.headline: Ancient statuette might be sign of Albania temple.

text.p: A solid gold statuette of the Greek goddess Artemis found in shallow waters off the Albanian coast could indicate the existence of an ancient temple nearby, a newspaper said on Wednesday.

The daily Gazeta Shqiptare said a teenage boy fished the golden figure, which stands 10 cm tall and weighs 50 grammes, out of water near the historic port of Durres, about 45 km (30 miles) west of Tirana.
The statue, found about 10 days ago, portrays Artemis as a huntress with a bow and a quiver of arrows.
The daily said the boy's family turned down an offer of $3,000 for the figure from a foreign collector and instead turned it over to local archaeologist, Hasan Ulqini.
Ulqini said the figure, believed to date back to the first century A.D., could possibly be testimony to the existence of a temple devoted to Artemis near Currilaj Beach north of Durres.
"Such a temple is cited in the books of ancient authors but up to now there is no archaeological testimony of its existence," the paper said.
Currilaj used to be a wealthy quarter of the 2,000 year-old port town of Durres.
